Figure 8:Qualitative ablation of DEM. Insets show the averaged attention from the target point to the source image. With DEM, it peaks closer to the handle and the edit is more precise.
Figure 9:Additional visual comparison with other models on DragBench and DragBench++. Target points are overlaid on the generated images to facilitate analysis of editing accuracy.

Figure 10:Grounding of textual coordinates. Each input image shows the queried normalized coordinate as a red point. Given the image and the coordinate, BAGEL often describes an unrelated object, whereasThinkDragidentifies the correct object and part at the queried location.
Figure 11:Comparison between DIFT-based and MLLM-based point tracking. MLLM-based tracking is more robust in challenging cases involving large structural changes or distractors.
